newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African wool prices rise at latest auction.
newsitem.headline: S.African wool prices rise at latest auction.

text.p: South African wool prices rose at the latest weekly auction, the Wool Board said.
It said 11,679 bales were offered at this week's sale, of which 99.3 percent was sold.

Price quotes for long Merino fleeces of 20 micron rose 4.4 percent, 21 micron rose 3.3 percent, 22 micron rose 4 percent, 23 micron rose 4.5 percent, 24 micron rose 4.2 percent and 25 micron rose 4.3 percent.

Prices for Merino bellies rose 10.3 percent, Merino lambs rose 5.8 percent and Merino locks rose 4.8 percent. The offering included 1,762 bales of other White Wools, 1,969 bales of Ciskei/Transkei, 1,774 bales of Lesotho and 1,100 bales of coarse and coloured.

Of the 20 and 25 micron offered, one hundred percent was sold. Of the 1,364 bales of 21 micron offered, 99.5 percent was sold. Of 2,312 bales of 22 micron offered, 99.9 percent was sold. 1,506 bales of 23 micron was offered, which sold 99.4 percent and of the 727 bales of 24 micron offered, 99.2 percent sold.
The next sale would take place on 6 November, when the offering would be 10,000 bales.
